- Windows quietly remembers apps (could be spy) that turned on your camera, even after you delete them

why you should do it today:

- a $40 spy tool bought in 100+ countries infected 500,000+ computers and could switch on their webcams remotely (US Departament of Justice)

Windows:

1. install repo below and type /camera-guard in Claude Code, it reads the hidden log of every app that ever turned on your camera and mic

2. delete AnyDesk, TeamViewer ot any remote app you don't use

3. Windows has a hidden "Camera on/off pop-up, off by default, ask Claude to turn it on and you see every time the camera starts

4. really shut camera off, Settings switch isn't enough:

• BIOS (strongest ): hold shift, click Restart - Troubleshoot → Advancedf options → UEFI Firmware Settings , set Camera to Disabled and add a BIOS password.

Windows can't see the camera at all. Need it for a call? - Turn it back on there. Not every laptop has it, Claude checks your model

• camera switch or key: some laptops have a slider on the side or an F-key with a crossed-out camera. Slide it off when you're not using it

• Device Manager → Cameras → Desible device: one click to undo (but any app with admin rights can undo it too)

5. run Microsoft Defender Offline, the deep scan built into Windows (Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → scan options): it restarts your PC and hunts hard-to-catch spyware before Windows starts

- an unknown app firing up the camera at night during sleep

- a $40 spy tool sold in 100+ countries hit 500,000+ computers and could flip their webcams on remotely (US Department of Justice)

- James Comey, while FBI director, covered his laptop camera with tape

Windows checklist:
1. Grab the repo below and run /camera-guard in Claude Code - it pulls up the hidden record of each app that has used camera or mic
2. Remove AnyDesk, TeamViewer or any remote tool you don't need
3. Windows ships a hidden pop-up for camera on/off that starts disabled - have Claude enable it, so every camera start shows up
4. Actually disable the camera, since the Settings toggle isn't enough:
- BIOS is the strongest: hold Shift, click Restart, then go Troubleshoot, Advanced options, UEFI Firmware Settings, disable Camera and set a BIOS password. Want it back for a call? Re-enable it in the same place. Not every laptop supports it - Claude checks your model
- a physical slider, or an F-key showing a struck-through camera: flip it off when idle
- Device Manager, Cameras, Disable device: one click to undo, though any app with admin rights can flip it back
5. Kick off a Microsoft Defender Offline scan from Windows Security, then Virus & threat protection: it reboots and hunts spyware before Windows loads

2. Under System Settings, go General, then Sharing, and switch off Remote Management, Remote Login and Screen Sharing

What I found:

• 7 bots on an hourly clock is 1,176 runs a week by my math, and most of them come back empty

• Bots that hand off through email leave you a pile of drafts, because every send waits for your approval

• A "test run" is not a test. It does the real work, so one wrong prompt can act for real

• One greedy bot can eat your whole X budget: 1,000 reads a day, 30 a minute, shared by everyone

• One launch hour with 250 signups on a single email alias breaks the 200 runs an hour cap

• And much more...

It's not just my setup:

- A single bot on a 5 minute clock is 2,016 runs a week, even if nothing ever happens (by my math)
- My launch team does the same job in about 60

How to fix yours:

1. Paste the prompt from the replies into Grok Bot
2. Keep 1 clock (Monday 09:00) and turn everything else into triggers: a bot starts only when the one before it writes DONE
3. Hand off through a shared LEDGER file, never email
4. Give every bot its own X reads budget and a hard STOP at the cap
5. Let only one bot touch money, with a $40 cap and your yes on every single buy

Do it before your next routine fires. Then read the full guide on all 7 bots below ↓

virals.name: noko
virals.text:
Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.  

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku and Opus 5.5 together, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Claude Code has a hidden flag that puts Opus 5.5 on call while Sonnet does the work:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

it's Anthropic's "advisor strategy", built right into Claude Code.

here's the split:

> Sonnet 5.5 runs the session and writes the code
> Haiku 5.5 subagents read files and docs in parallel
> Opus 5.5 sits on call and reads the whole transcript when asked
> you stop paying Opus rates for routine turns

Opus usually steps in at three moments:

> before a plan locks
> when the same error shows up twice
> before calling the task done

Sonnet builds. Haiku explores. Opus reviews.

Anthropic's own numbers: Sonnet + Opus advisor scored 2.7 points higher on SWE-bench Multilingual than Sonnet alone, at 11.9% lower cost per task.

the full tree
> main session: Sonnet 5.5, edits code
> search: Haiku 5.5, maps the repo
> grep: Haiku 5.5, finds call sites
> docs: Haiku 5.5, pulls the API reference
> advisor: Opus 5.5, reads everything when consulted

paste this into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Make Sonnet my main model and set Opus as my advisor (advisorModel: opus).
2. Create three read-only subagents on Haiku 5.5: search (maps the repo), grep (finds call sites), docs (pulls the API reference).
3. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: consult the advisor before locking a plan, after the same error twice, and before calling a task done.
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."

where it breaks, from my own runs:

> --advisor haiku on a Sonnet session gets refused. it keeps running with no advisor
> on a one-line question, the single Opus call cost 3x the whole Sonnet part
> it's still marked experimental and doesn't show up in claude --help

worth it for long refactors and bugs that keep coming back. skip it for quick questions.

outsiders.text:
Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.  

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku and Opus 5.5 together, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Claude Code has a hidden flag that puts Opus 5.5 on call while Sonnet does the work:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

it's Anthropic's "advisor strategy", built right into Claude Code.
